principle: A known tax acronym or polysemous tax phrase is not automatically tax when surrounding words establish a different object, field, role or meaning.
diagnosedMechanism: All 67 material false allows and all 12 metamorphic false-allow failures fired with reason strong_tax_signal. STRONG_TAX_SIGNAL_PATTERNS matches unconditionally except for the R18 cosignal-defeatable NON_TAX_OBJECT_VETO_PATTERNS tier. Two sub-defects: (1) no veto pattern existed at all for many non-tax object families; (2) TAX_COSIGNAL_PATTERNS wrongly included bare 2-4 letter acronyms (RMC, RMO), and phrase cosignals could match as a substring anywhere and defeat a veto match anywhere else with no role-based judgment.

software_code_ui_role.description: The sentence's true subject is a variable, function, form field, console output, design/colour/hue token, icon, CSS class, plugin, software flag, app log or code snippet — not a tax concept.
examples: subject to VAT as variable name in code
input VAT as form input label
software_code_ui_role.remedy: dominant non-tax role veto, software/code/UI family

random_unknown_code_label.description: A tax acronym is explicitly relabeled as a random/unknown project, product, training or course code, or a field abbreviation.
examples: Use RCIT as a course code.
random_unknown_code_label.remedy: dominant non-tax role veto, random/unknown code label family

culture_tradition.description: 'customs' or a tax-shaped word used in its ordinary cultural/social/traditional sense.
examples: What local customs apply at dinner?
culture_tradition.remedy: dominant non-tax role veto, culture/tradition family

audio_music.description: BOC/RMC/capital gain/etc. used in a music, audio or amplifier context.
examples: What is capital gain on an amplifier?
Is BOC a band of chords?
audio_music.remedy: dominant non-tax role veto, audio/music family

physical_device.description: FAN/PAN/OSD used for an actual cooling fan, cooking utensil or on-screen display.
physical_device.remedy: dominant non-tax role veto, physical device family

physical_animal.remedy: dominant non-tax role veto, physical/animal family

medicine.description: 'prescriptive/prescription period' or 'deficiency' used in a medical sense.
medicine.remedy: dominant non-tax role veto, medicine family

real_estate_marketing.description: 'gross estate' used for real-estate marketing copy or landscaping, not estate tax.
real_estate_marketing.remedy: dominant non-tax role veto, real-estate/marketing family

hobby_game.description: Tax phrase reused inside a board game, game guild or quest.
examples: transfer pricing in a board game
registered business enterprise as a game guild
import duty in a game quest
hobby_game.remedy: dominant non-tax role veto, hobby/game family

school_class.description: Tax phrase reused for a school raffle, exam grade, grammar class, negotiation class, or a plain alphabetical list.
examples: gross receipts for a school raffle
school_class.remedy: dominant non-tax role veto, school/class family

architecture_building.description: 'permanent establishment' used in architecture, or 'Bureau of Customs' used only for building directions.
examples: Bureau of Customs as building directions only
architecture_building.remedy: dominant non-tax role veto, architecture/building family

office_generic_mislabel.description: Tax term reused for a novel list, a generic conference agenda without a BIR/notice-for qualifier, or negotiation class.
examples: books of accounts as novel list
office_generic_mislabel.remedy: dominant non-tax role veto, office/generic mislabel family

explicit_negation.description: The sentence explicitly negates tax relevance.
explicit_negation.remedy: dominant non-tax role veto, explicit negation family

false_refusal_weak_signal_underfit.description: Coherent tax phrases carried only as weak/CLARIFY signals rather than strong anchors.
false_refusal_weak_signal_underfit.remedy: add or strengthen a strong-signal anchor for the coherent phrase; not a veto change
